cards.objective: Explain the lower position of the right kidney.
cards.front: Why does the right kidney lie lower than the left?

why.t: The left kidney is at about T12 to L3; the right is lower, pushed down by the liver. They lie either side of the spine, behind the peritoneum, protected by muscle, fat and ribs.

simpler.t: Your kidneys clean your blood and turn the waste into urine.

depth.t: Cortex: the lighter outer region, holding all the renal corpuscles and convoluted tubules.
Medulla: the inner region, with renal pyramids and papillae.
Renal pelvis: the funnel formed from the calyces; it narrows into the ureter.
Hilum: where vessels, nerves, lymphatics and the ureter enter and leave.
Capsule and fat: a fibrous capsule, a cushioning fat pad and renal fascia surround each kidney.

clinical.t: Kidney failure. Failing kidneys make too little erythropoietin and active vitamin D.

trap.t: The kidneys are retroperitoneal: behind the peritoneum, not inside the peritoneal cavity.

cards.source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport; 25.3 Gross Anatomy of the Kidney; 25.10; 17.10
